Now, therefore, the Government of
Pakistan is pleased to make the following Order:-
8. Substitution of section 4A, Northern
Areas Council Legal Framework Order, 1994.-In the said Order, for section
4A, the following new section shall be substituted, namely:--
"4A. Election of Speaker and Deputy
Speaker.-(1) After a general election, the Assembly, at its first meeting and to
the exclusion of any other business, elect from amongst its members a Speaker
and a Deputy Speaker and, so often as the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker
becomes vacant, the Assembly shall elect another member as Speaker or, as the
case may be, Deputy Speaker.
(2) The Speaker and Deputy Speaker shall
be entitled to the status, salary and perquisites as the Government may, by
notification in the official Gazette, determine.
(3) When the office of Speaker is vacant
or the Speaker is unable to perform his functions for any reason, the Deputy
Speaker shall act as Speaker, and if, at any time, the Deputy Speaker is also
absent or for any reason is unable to act as Speaker, such member as may be
determined by the rules of procedure of the Assembly shall preside at the
meeting of the Assembly.
(4) The Speaker or the Deputy Speaker
shall not preside at a meeting of the Assembly when a resolution for his
removal from office is being considered. In such situation a member from the
panel announced by the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker shall preside the meeting
of the Assembly.
4AA. Resignation of Speaker and Deputy
Speaker.-(1) The Speaker or Deputy Speaker may, by writing under his hand
addressed to the Chairman Northern Areas, resign his office.
(2) When the Assembly is dissolved, the
Speaker shall continue in his office till the person elected to fill the office
by the next Assembly enters upon his office.".

Pakistan is pleased to make the following Order:-
10. Insertion of new sections 4C, 4D and 4E,
Northern Areas Council Legal Framework Order, 1994.-In the said Order,
after section 4B, the following new sections shall be inserted, namely:-
"4C. Adviser performing
functions of Chief Executive.-(1) In case the office of the Chief
Executive becomes vacant by reason of death, resignation or his ceasing to be
member of the Assembly or for any other reason the Chairman Northern Areas may
nominate an Adviser to perform the functions of that office and shall continue
in office until a new Chief Executive is elected and enters upon his office.
(2) If the Assembly is in session at the
time when the Chief Executive resigns his office, or in the event of death of
the Chief Executive, the Assembly shall forthwith proceed to elect a Chief
Executive, and if the Assembly is not in session, the Speaker shall, for that
purpose, summon it to meet within fourteen days of the vacation of
office.".
4D. Vote of no-confidence against Chief
Executive, Speaker and Deputy Speaker.-(l) A resolution for a vote of no-confidence
moved by not less than twenty per cent of the total membership of Assembly may
be passed against the Chief Executive, the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker, as
the case may be, by the Assembly.
(2) A resolution referred to in
subsection (1) shall not be voted upon before the expiration of three days, or
later than seven days, from the day on which such resolution is moved in the
Assembly.
(3) If the resolution referred to in
subsection (1) is passed by two-thirds majority of total membership of the Assembly,
the Chief Executive, the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker, as the case may be,
shall cease to hold office:
Provided that if the resolution referred
to in subsection (1) is not passed no such resolution shall be moved until a
period of one year has elapsed."

PART-I
NORTHERN AREAS
SUPREME APPELLATE COURT
21. Northern Areas Supreme Appellate Court.-(1)
There shall be a Northern Areas Supreme
Appellate Court which shall consist of a Chief Judge and two Judges.
(2) The Government, in consultation with the
Chief Judge, may from time to time increase or decrease the number of Judges.
Explanation.-In this part,-
(a) the
expression Chief Judge means the Chief Judge of the Northern Areas Supreme
Appellate Court; and
(b) the
expression "Judge" means the Judge of the Northern Areas Supreme
Appellate Court.

PART-I
NORTHERN AREAS
SUPREME APPELLATE COURT
22. Appointment of Chief Judge and Judge.--(1)
The Chief Judge and Judges shall be appointed by the Government for a term not
exceeding three years and may be appointed for such further term as the
Government may determine.
(2) A person shall not be appointed as
Chief Judge unless-
(a) he has been a Judge of a Supreme
Court of Pakistan or is qualified to be a Judge of the Supreme Court of
Pakistan; or
(b) has for a period of, or for periods
aggregating not less than fifteen years practised law
as an Advocate before the Chief Court in the Northern Areas or a High Court of
any part of Pakistan; or
(c) has for a
period of not less than fifteen years held a judicial office.
(3) A person shall not be appointed as
Judge unless he has been the Chief Judge of the Northern Areas Chief Court or a Judge of a High
Court of any part of Pakistan.

28. Appellate jurisdiction.-(1) The
Northern Areas Supreme Appellate Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and
determine appeals from judgments, decrees, final orders or sentences of the
Chief Court for Northern Areas.
(2) An appeal shall lie to the Northern
Areas Supreme Appellate Court from any judgment, decree, final order or
sentence of the Chief Court
for Northern Areas-
(a) if the Chief Court for Northern Areas
has on appeal reversed an order of acquittal of an accused person and sentenced
him to death or to imprisonment for life, or on revision, has enhanced a
sentence to a sentence as aforesaid; or
(b) if the Chief Court for Northern Areas
has withdrawn for trial before itself any case from any Court subordinate to it
and has in such trial convicted the accused person and sentenced him as
aforesaid; or
(c) if the Chief Court for
Northern Areas has imposed any punishment on any person for its contempt; or
(d) if the
amount or value of the subject matter of the dispute in the court of first
instance was. and also in dispute in appeal is, not less than fifty thousand
rupees or such other sum as may be specified in that behalf by Act of the
Assembly and the judgment, decree or final order appealed from has varied or
set aside the judgment, decree or final order of the court immediately below;
or
(e) if the judgment, decree or final
order involves directly or in directly some claim or question respecting
property of the like amount or value and the judgment, decree or final order
appealed from has varied or set aside the judgment, decree or final order of
the court immediately below; or
(f) if the Chief Court for
Northern Areas certifies that the case involves a substantial question of law
as to the interpretation of this Order.
(3) An appeal to the Northern Areas
Supreme Appellate Court from a judgment, decree, order or sentence of the Chief
Court for Northern Areas in a case to which sub-Article (2) does not apply
shall lie only if the Northern Areas Supreme Appellate Court grants leave to appeal.

36. Contempt of Court.-( 1) In this section
"Court" means the Northern Areas Supreme Appellate Court or Chief
Court for Northern Areas.
(2)
A Court shall have power to punish any persons
who-
(a) abuses,
interferes with or obstructs the process of the Court in any way or disobeys
any order of the Court.
(b) scandalizes
the Court or otherwise does anything which tends to bring the Court or a Judge
of the Court into hatred, ridicule or contempt;
(c) does
anything which tends to prejudice the determination of a matter pending before
the Court; or
(d) does any
other thing which, by law, constitute, contempt of the Court.
(3) The exercise of the powers conferred
on a Court by this section may be regulated by law and, subject to law, by
rules made by the Court.

NORTHERN AREAS

37. Supreme Judicial Committee.-(1) There shall be a Supreme Judicial Committee for Northern
Areas, in this section referred to as the Committee.
(2) The Committee shall consist of-
(a) Chief Judge, Supreme Appellate Court;
(b) the most
senior Judge of Supreme Appellate Court;
(c) Chief Judge, Chief Court for Northern Areas; and
(d) Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice
and Human Rights.
(3) If at any time the Committee is
inquiring into the capacity or conduct of a Judge who is a member of the
Committee, or a member of the Committee is absent or is unable to act due to
illness or any other cause, then if such member is Judge of Supreme Appellate
Court or is the Chief Judge of the Chief Court for Northern Areas, the Judge of
the Supreme Appellate Court or the Judge of the Chief Court for Northern Areas,
as the case may be, who is next in seniority shall act as member of the
Committee.
(4) The Chief Judge of Supreme Appellate
Court shall act as Chairman of the Committee and in case of proceedings against
the Chief Judge of Supreme Appellate Court the most Senior Judge of the Supreme
Appellate Court shall act as Chairman of the Committee and the next Judge in
seniority of the Supreme Appellate Court shall act as member of the Committee.
(5) If, upon any matter inquired into by
the Committee, there is a difference of opinion amongst its members, the
opinion of the majority shall prevail, and the report of the Committee to the
Government shall be expressed in terms of the view of the majority.
(6) If, on information from any source,
the Committee or the Government is of the opinion that a Judge or Chief Judge
of Supreme Appellate Court or a Judge or Chief Judge of Chief Court for
Northern Areas-
(a) may be
incapable of properly performing the duties of his office by reason of physical
or mental incapacity ; or
(b) may have
been guilty of misconduct, the Government shall direct the Committee to, or the
Committee may, on its own motion, inquire into the matter.
(7) If, after inquiring into the matter,
the Committee reports to the Government that it is of the opinion-
(a) that the
Judge is incapable of performing the duties of his office or has been guilty of
misconduct; and
(b) that he
should be removed from office, the Government may remove the Judge from office.
(8) A Judge of the Supreme Appellate
Court or of a Chief Court
shall not be removed from office except as provided by this section.
(9) The Committee shall issue a code of
conduct to be observed by Chief Judges and Judges of the Supreme Appellate
Court and of the Chief Court.
(10) The Committee may regulate its own
procedure.
(11) The provisions of Article 36
relating to contempt shall apply as they apply to the Chief Court and the Supreme Appellate
Court.

45. Jurisdiction.--(1) The Chief Court
shall have the jurisdiction and exercise the powers vested in a High Court
under the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and any law
applicable to Northern Areas and shall not have jurisdiction save as is
hereinafter conferred.
(2) The Chief Court may, if it is
satisfied that no adequate remedy is provided by law, on the application of any
aggrieved person, make an order giving such direction to any person or
authority exercising any power or performing any functions in, or in relation
to, any territory within the jurisdiction of that Court as may be appropriate
for the enforcement of any of the Fundamental Rights specified in Chapter I of
Part II of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan as conferred by
section 19A.
(3) An order shall not be made under
sub-Article (2) on application made by or in relation to a person who is a
member of the Armed Forces of Pakistan, or who is for the time being subject to
any law relating to any of those Forces, in respect of his terms and conditions
of his service, in respect of any matter arising out of service, or in respect
of any action taken in relation to him as a member of the Armed Forces of
Pakistan or as a person subject to such law.

S.R.O.1231(I)/2007,
dated 15-12-2007.---Whereas it is expedient further to amend the Northern Areas
Council Legal Framework Order, 1994, for the purposes hereinafter appearing;
Now, therefore, the Government of
Pakistan is pleased to make the following Order:-
CHAPTER-3
MISCELLANEOUS
54. Repeal and savings.-(1) Subject to
sub-Articles (2) and (3), the Northern Areas Chief Court (Establishment) Order,
1998 and the Northern Areas Court of Appeals (Establishment) Order, 1999 are
hereby repealed.
(2) Any judgment given, sentence or decree
passed, decision or order made or any appeal, suit, application, or other
proceedings instituted or pending before-
(a) Chief Court for
Northern Areas; or
(b) Northern Areas Court of Appeals
established under the Orders referred to in
sub-Article (2) shall be deemed to have been given, passed, made by, or
instituted before, the Chief Court for Northern Areas or, as the case may be,
the Northern Areas Supreme Appellate Court, established under this Order and it
shall not be necessary for the aforesaid courts to record any evidence or
re-hear any witness for the decision of any pending matter.
(3) The Chairman and members of the Chief
Court for Northern Areas
and the Northern Areas Court
of Appeals referred to in
sub-Article (2) shall continue and shall be deemed to have been appointed as
the Chief Judges and Judges of the Chief Court for Northern Areas and the
Northern Areas Supreme Appellate Court established under this Order, as the
case may be, subject to their respective tenure and terms and conditions provided
in pursuance of the Orders referred to in sub-Article (2).".

55. Amendment of Schedule I, Northern Areas
Council Legal Framework Order, 1994.-In the said Order, in Schedule I,-
(a) in Form 'A', for the words
"Chairman, Chief Court", the words "Chief Judge, Supreme
Appellate Court" shall be substituted; and
(b) after Form~
'E' the following new Forms shall be added, namely:-
FORM "F"
OATH OF OFFICE OF THE
DEPUTY SPEAKER
NORTHERN AREAS
LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY
[Article 11(3)]
I ...being the Deputy Speaker of
the Northern Areas Legislative Assembly, do solemnly swear that I will bear
true faith and allegiance to Pakistan and uphold the sovereignty and integrity
of Pakistan;
That, as Deputy Speaker of the Northern
Areas Legislative Assembly, I will be faithful to the declaration of the
Founder of Pakistan Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah
that Pakistan
would be a democratic State based on Islamic principles of social justice;
That I will perform my functions honestly
and faithfully;
That I shall strive to preserve the
Islamic Ideology which is the basis for the creation of Pakistan;
That I shall strive to preserve and to
maintain religious/sectarian harmony in the Northern Areas and shall not
indulge in any activity prejudicial to this cause; and
That I will not directly or indirectly
communicate or reveal to any person any official secret which may come
to my knowledge as Deputy Speaker of the Northern Areas Legislative Assembly.
Form "G"
(See Articles 24 and 39)
OATH OF OFFICE OF
CHIEF JUDGE AND JUDGES
(In the name of Allah,
the most Beneficent, the most Merciful.)
I,_______________do solemnly swear that I will bear true faith and allegiance to Pakistan and uphold the sovereignty and
integrity of Pakistan:
That, as Chief Judge of
the Northern Areas Supreme Appellate Court (or a Judge of the Northern Areas
Supreme Appellate Court or Chief Judge or a Judge of the Chief Court for the Northern Areas).
I will discharge my duties,
and perform my
functions, honestly, to the
best of my ability, and faithfully, in accordance with this Order and the law:
That I will abide by the code of conduct
issued by the Supreme Judicial Committee for Northern Areas:
That I will not allow my personal
interest to influence my official conduct or my official decisions:
And that, in all
circumstances, I will do right to all manner of people, according to law,
without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.
[May Allah Almighty help me guide me (A'meen).]"
